newsitem.title: FRANCE: French flights to be cut by two-day strike.
newsitem.headline: French flights to be cut by two-day strike.

text.p: A strike by pilots, engineers and stewards will sharply cut French flights on Wednesday and Thursday, adding to transport problems as the nation is gripped by a stoppage by truckers.

Air unions reaffirmed their calls for a two-day strike over grievances including restructurings, feared job cuts and widening competition. They said, however, that they had made some progress in talks with the centre-right government.
Air France said it would guarantee two-thirds of long-haul flights and a quarter of medium-haul flights over the two days.
The airline's short-haul Air France Europe said it expected to cut more than half its flights. It said it would guarantee 213 flights on Wednesday and 200 on Thursday, against 480 normally each day.
Smaller airlines Air Liberte and privately-owned AOM, owned by the state-backed CDR holding company, forecast they would be able to maintain all their flights over the two days.
The unions saw some signs of hope in talks with Transport Minister Bernard Pons on Monday.
They said in statement they had "noted some progress, notably in terms of reducing distortions of competition. Nevertheless, nothing allows us to call off the strike".
The strikes, first called almost two weeks ago, will add to transport problems in France. A nine-day-old strike by truckers is strangling French highways and fuel supplies with road blockades.
